newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH SHARES EASE 0.49 PCT IN THIN VOLUME.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH SHARES EASE 0.49 PCT IN THIN VOLUME.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell slightly in lower volume and weak sentiment on Friday due to lack of market moving expectations and liquidity inflow, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 2,040, down 10 points, or 0.49 percent from Thursday's all-time high close of 2,050. It hit a trading record of 2,070 at the opening.
Daily trade volume shrank by 26.7 percent to 18.29 trillion lira from Thursday's 24.95 trillion.

Brokers said the midday funeral of bourse chairman Tuncay Artun who died on Wednesday at the age of 48, further depressed traders and officials, causing trade to become extremely sullen in the afternoon.
The opening of the second session was delayed to 1230 GMT instead of the regular 1100 GMT because of the funeral.

"There was sadness in the market after the funeral which affected the transactions. There were also sales by players who did not want to carry their positions to Monday," said one dealer from Garanti Securities.
Some brokers said the market's failure to pierce resistance at the index's 2,060-070 levels since the beginning of the week caused prices to revert back.

Of the 251 shares traded, losers outdid gainers by 106 to 75 and 70 finished steady. The IMKB Industrial eased 0.86 percent to 1,969, the IMKB Services edged up 0.15 percent to 1,996 and the IMKB Financial edged 0.18 percent down to 2,213.

The most active stocks were largely state-owned flat steel producer Eregli, down 500 lira at 28,000, Dogan Holding, up 50 lira at 4,450 and steel rope, wire producer Celik Halat, up 350 lira to 5,500.
The three made up 24 percent of the total turnover.

Media and finance group Dogan Sirketler Grubu Holding bought on Friday 50.53 percent of Celik Halat ve Tel Sanayi for $21.05 million in final negotiations of a tender organised by Turkish sequestration and bankruptcy authorities.
The Celik Halat stake was put on sale earlier this year after owner AOG Turkinvest brokerage house went bankrupt during the 1994 financial and economic crisis.
The exchange briefly halted trade in Celik Halat shares in the afternoon to receive the tender results.
